act_vs_pred: Compares the model's predictions (y-axis) against the actual target values (x-axis). A perfect model would have all points precisely on the diagonal line. Points above the line are over-predicted, points below are under-predicted.
res_dist: Shows the histogram of residuals (errors). A well-behaved linear model usually has symmetrically distributed residuals centered around zero, closely matching the normal curve.
res_vs_pred: Plots residuals against predicted values. Used to detect heteroscedasticity. A healthy model shows a random scatter of points with constant variance, not a 'funnel' or 'fan' shape.
res_vs_act: Plots residuals against actual values. Helps visualize how the prediction error behaves across the true range of the target variable. Systemic patterns here suggest missing non-linear relationships.
qq: Quantile-Quantile plot compares the distribution of residuals to a theoretical Normal distribution. If residuals are normally distributed, points should closely follow the diagonal reference line.
scale_loc: Plots the square root of absolute standardized residuals against predicted values. Focuses on checking the 'constant variance' (homoscedasticity) assumption without being affected by the sign of the error.
post_pred: Compares the kernel density estimate of the actual values vs. the predicted values. Helps check if the model captures the overall shape, modality, and spread of the true data distribution.
linearity: Checks the linearity assumption with a LOWESS smoothing curve over the residuals. If the trend line deviates heavily from zero, the relationship might be non-linear.
leverage: Identifies influential observations. Points with high leverage (x-axis) and high residuals (y-axis) fall outside the dashed Cook's Distance contours and have a disproportionate, potentially harmful impact on the model's fit.
vif: Variance Inflation Factor (VIF) measures multicollinearity. Values above 5-10 suggest high correlation between features, which can destabilize model coefficients and interpretability.
outliers: Displays the distribution of feature values grouped by the magnitude of the model's error (Low vs High Residuals). Helps identify if specific feature ranges are systematically responsible for the worst errors.
metrics: A summary of standard performance metrics (Accuracy, F1-Score, Precision, Recall, etc.) for the classification model.
cm: A matrix showing True Positives, False Positives, True Negatives, and False Negatives. The diagonal represents correct predictions, while off-diagonals are errors.
class_dist: Displays the proportion and exact count of instances belonging to each target class. Helps identify class imbalance, which can strongly bias the model.
prob_dist: Shows the distribution of the model's predicted probabilities. Ideally, predictions should cluster sharply near 0% or 100%, indicating high model confidence rather than uncertainty (clustering near 50%).
roc: Receiver Operating Characteristic curve illustrates the tradeoff between True Positive Rate and False Positive Rate across different probability thresholds. Higher Area Under Curve (AUC) indicates better separability.
pr: Precision-Recall curve focuses on the tradeoff between positive predictive value and sensitivity. Specially useful and more informative than ROC for highly imbalanced datasets.
misclass: Highlights the density of feature values grouped by outcome (Correctly Predicted vs. Misclassified). Useful to spot structural feature boundaries where the model systematically fails.
